findings.proposition: Advance Flex as the broad-audience development priority, while retaining Plus: Flex leads on appeal but has no demonstrated purchase-intent advantage over Plus. Weighted appeal is 61.0% versus 54.0% (+7.0 percentage points; Holm p=0.0112), meeting the 5-point commercial threshold. Purchase intent is 53.2% versus 50.4% (+2.8 points; Holm p=0.311).
findings.claim_strength: Recommendation supported by a significant, commercially material appeal advantage; purchase-intent superiority is unproven.
findings.qualification: Each concept has n=700; effective bases are 650.1 for Flex and 645.6 for Plus. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence. Purchase intent assumes a reasonable price and is not observed demand.

findings.proposition: Advance Plus for further testing among food explorers. Explorer appeal is 72.1% for Plus versus 60.1% for Flex; purchase intent is 63.9% versus 52.4%. Among non-explorers, the pattern reverses: appeal is 48.4% versus 61.2%, and purchase intent 46.2% versus 53.5%. The pre-specified differences in the Plus-minus-Flex gaps are 24.85 points for appeal (Holm p=0.0000137) and 18.81 points for purchase intent (Holm p=0.000968).
findings.claim_strength: Confirmatory evidence of heterogeneity supports a targeted development recommendation.
findings.qualification: Explorer bases: Plus n=234, effective n=223.5; Flex n=236, effective n=225.4. Non-explorer bases: Plus n=466, effective n=449.1; Flex n=464, effective n=446.3. Interaction tests establish that relative performance differs between groups; they are not adjusted tests of superiority within each group. Explorer status was defined before exposure as mean food-orientation agreement >=4.

findings.proposition: Prioritise clearer communication and a more believable, relevant proposition when developing Plus. Flex exceeds Plus on understanding (95.7% versus 32.3%; +63.5 points), credibility (62.3% versus 42.2%; +20.1), and relevance (63.7% versus 49.4%; +14.3); all Holm p<0.000001. Expected value for money does not distinguish them: 56.3% for Flex versus 56.7% for Plus (Holm p=0.900).
findings.claim_strength: Significant, commercially material diagnostic differences; proposed improvements are hypotheses to test.
findings.qualification: Full assigned-cell bases are n=700 per concept. These results do not establish that improving understanding, credibility or relevance would increase appeal or purchase intent. Value for money assumes a modest premium; it does not measure willingness to pay a specific price.

findings.proposition: Preserve Plus's distinctiveness while addressing its mixed reception. Uniqueness reaches 81.4%, versus 47.9% for Flex and 34.3% for Simple: advantages of 33.5 and 47.1 points respectively, both Holm p<0.000001. Its appeal distribution contains both more maximum ratings than Flex (31.3% versus 26.7%) and more bottom-two ratings (23.8% versus 16.4%), despite its lower overall top-two appeal.
findings.claim_strength: Confirmed uniqueness advantages; descriptive evidence of a more divided appeal distribution.
findings.qualification: Each concept has n=700. Maximum-rating and bottom-two differences have no supplied adjusted tests and are descriptive. Distinctiveness alone does not establish demand or explain the audience interaction.

findings.proposition: Treat Plus's strong premium-conviction result as conditional evidence. Among respondents eligible for the routed question, top-two premium conviction is 78.8% for Plus, 50.1% for Flex and 37.7% for Simple. Plus's differences are statistically significant in the supplied comparisons, but only 69.0% of its assigned cell qualified, compared with 99.1% for Flex and 99.7% for Simple.
findings.claim_strength: Strong conditional descriptive result; unsuitable as evidence of unconditional premium superiority.
findings.qualification: Eligibility requires understanding_5 >=3, including the midpoint. Eligible bases: Plus n=483, effective n=444.4; Flex n=694, effective n=644.6; Simple n=698, effective n=643.4. Routing rates are unweighted; outcome percentages use wt_final. Selection occurs after concept exposure and differs sharply across concepts, so randomisation does not ensure comparable routed populations. Excluded responses are not failures or zeros.

findings.proposition: Deprioritise Simple in its current form. Appeal is 41.1%, below Flex by 19.9 points and Plus by 12.9; purchase intent is 40.4%, below Flex by 12.8 and Plus by 10.0. All four differences meet the commercial threshold and have Holm p<0.001. Simple is nevertheless easy to understand (92.9%) and credible (57.3%); these strengths have not translated into competitive primary outcomes.
findings.claim_strength: Consistent significant and commercially material disadvantages on both primary outcomes support deprioritisation.
findings.qualification: Each concept has n=700; Simple effective n=645.2. Flex's 2.8-point understanding advantage over Simple is significant (Holm p=0.0297) but below the commercial threshold. Its 4.9-point credibility lead is neither significant (Holm p=0.0690) nor commercially material. The recommendation concerns the tested concept, not every possible simplicity proposition.

beats.headline_intent: Prioritise Flex for broad development and deprioritise Simple; keep Plus under consideration.
beats.analytical_relationship: Primary outcomes establish the portfolio priorities while leaving Flex-versus-Plus purchase superiority unresolved.

beats.headline_intent: Give Plus a targeted development path among food explorers.
beats.analytical_relationship: Pre-specified interaction evidence qualifies the total-audience result and identifies a different relative response by audience.

beats.headline_intent: Retain Plus's distinctiveness while testing clearer, more relevant and credible communication.
beats.analytical_relationship: Diagnostic strengths and weaknesses inform development hypotheses without claiming causal drivers.

beats.headline_intent: Keep the premium claim conditional on who answered.
beats.analytical_relationship: Unequal post-exposure routing limits how strongly premium conviction can support advancement.

method_notes: Only the supplied study materials and analysis tables were used. No raw-data analysis was performed; analysis_claims is therefore empty. Evidence references use exact paths within analysis_results.json, with zero-based array indices.

This fictional randomised monadic study covers 2,100 UK adults aged 18–64 open to meal-kit use in the next 12 months, with 700 assigned to each concept. It provides no real market or customer validation.

Outcome percentages use wt_final and valid question bases. Top-two-box means ratings 4–5; bottom-two-box means 1–2. Full ordinal distributions inform interpretation; means are secondary and were not used to rank concepts.
Full-cell weighted totals are Flex 703.52, Plus 696.32 and Simple 700.16; Kish effective bases are 650.13, 645.63 and 645.23 respectively. Weighted totals are not respondent counts.

Supplied inference uses Kish effective-sample-size Wald comparisons of independent cells, with Holm adjustment across three concept pairs within each metric. Alpha is 0.05; correction is not across every metric in the report.

The two pre-specified Plus-minus-Flex interactions were Holm-adjusted together. Food explorer is the sole confirmatory strategic subgroup; exploratory demographic cuts were not used for headline recommendations.

Statistical significance and commercial materiality are separate: the declared materiality threshold is an absolute top-two difference of at least 5 percentage points. A numerical lead or nonsignificant difference does not establish superiority or equivalence.

Figures are rounded for readability; inference follows the supplied unrounded tables. Advancement means further concept development and testing, not a launch recommendation or proof of commercial success.
